question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The students were diligently / studying for their exams / for weeks before you arrived.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The students were diligently.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes an action that continued over a period ("for weeks") before another past action ("before you arrived"). This requires the past perfect continuous tense — "had been studying" — not the simple past continuous "were studying".

◦ Correct: The students had been diligently studying for their exams for weeks before you arrived.

• The error therefore lies in the segment "The students were diligently", where "were" should be "had been".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "studying for their exams" and "for weeks before you arrived" are correct.

• The time marker "for weeks before you arrived" signals a duration completed before a past point — a classic trigger for the past perfect continuous.

NOTE

• Past perfect continuous = had been + verb-ing. It shows an action that was going on for some time up to a certain point in the past (had been working, had been waiting, had been studying).

question: Identify the ANTONYM pair.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Dissuade and Encourage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dissuade" means to persuade someone NOT to do something (हतोत्साहित करना), whereas "Encourage" means to persuade someone TO do something / to give support (प्रोत्साहित करना). They are opposite in meaning, so they form an antonym pair.

◦ Example: She tried to dissuade him from quitting, while his friends encouraged him to stay.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Encourage and Support", Option 2 "Influence and Motivate" and Option 3 "Convince and Persuade" are all synonym pairs (words with similar meanings).

NOTE

• Antonyms of encourage: dissuade, discourage, deter. Synonyms of encourage: motivate, inspire, support, urge.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The artist believes that this new collection of paintings / has being / a masterpiece that / will redefine contemporary art.
option_1: The artist believes that this new collection of paintings
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. has being.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "has being" is grammatically wrong. After "collection" (a singular subject), a finite verb is needed. The correct form is "is" (present tense) — "this new collection ... is a masterpiece".

◦ Correct: The artist believes that this new collection of paintings is a masterpiece that will redefine contemporary art.

• "being" is the present participle/gerund of "be" and cannot follow "has" here to make a correct verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other three segments are grammatically correct.

• "has been" (present perfect) would need a complement too, but the natural, correct link here is the simple present "is a masterpiece".

NOTE

• Do not confuse "being" (participle/gerund) with "been" (past participle). "has been" is valid; "has being" is always incorrect.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The students demonstrated their excitement by volunteering for community service.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. enthusiasm.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Excitement" means a feeling of great eagerness, energy and interest. Its closest synonym is "enthusiasm" (keen interest and eagerness). (उत्साह)

◦ Example: The children showed great excitement/enthusiasm on the school trip.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "anxiety" (worry/nervousness) is nearly an antonym.

• Option 2 "ignorance" (lack of knowledge) and Option 3 "freedom" (liberty) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of excitement: enthusiasm, eagerness, exhilaration, zeal, thrill. Antonyms: boredom, apathy, indifference.

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word in the given sentence.

Polluted air can be dangeros, even if the pollutants are invisible.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. dangerous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt word is "dangerous", meaning likely to cause harm or injury. (खतरनाक)

◦ Correct: Polluted air can be dangerous, even if the pollutants are invisible.

• Spelling key: DANGER + OUS.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "dangerus", "dangeres" and "dangeris" are all misspelt forms; the adjective is formed by adding the suffix "-ous" to "danger".

NOTE

• Adjectives ending in "-ous" (full of / having): dangerous, famous, courageous, nervous, various. The noun is "danger"; the adjective is "dangerous".

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Which flower do you like best?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the best.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When choosing from more than two things ("Which flower ..."), the superlative degree with 'the' is used — "the best".

◦ Correct: Which flower do you like the best?

• "best" is the superlative of "good/well" (good – better – best).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "good" (positive) is incorrect in a comparison of many.

• Option 2 "most good" is wrong — "good" is irregular and never takes "most".

• Option 3 "better" (comparative) is used only when comparing two items.

NOTE

• Degrees of "good": good – better (two things) – the best (three or more). Never form "gooder/goodest" or "more/most good".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase.

I should look into my past and decide what the next course of action should be.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Retrospect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To "look into my past" means to look back on / review past events — that is "retrospect" (to consider something that has already happened). (अतीत पर दृष्टि डालना / पूर्वावलोकन)

◦ Example: In retrospect, I realise I should have studied harder.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Prospect" means an outlook for the future, not the past.

• Option 2 "Introspect" means to examine one's own thoughts/feelings (looking inward), not one's past events specifically.

• Option 3 "Disrespect" (lack of respect) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Prefix "retro-" = backward/back (retrospect, retrograde, retroactive). "pro-" = forward (prospect, progress); "intro-" = inward (introspect, introvert).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Timid
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Bold.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Timid" means shy, fearful and lacking courage. Its antonym is "bold", meaning brave, fearless and confident. (डरपोक का विलोम — निडर/साहसी)

◦ Example: The timid boy slowly became bold after joining the debate club.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Oppress" (to treat harshly) is unrelated.

• Options 3 "Modest" and 4 "Humble" (both meaning unassuming/not proud) are closer to synonyms of timid than antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of timid: shy, nervous, fearful, cowardly, meek. Antonyms: bold, brave, confident, daring, fearless.

question:
The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

His aunt who lives at America brought a lot of gifts for him and his sister.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. in America brought a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Before the name of a large area / country, the correct preposition is "in", not "at". So "lives at America" should be "lives in America".

◦ Correct: His aunt who lives in America brought a lot of gifts for him and his sister.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "His aunt which lives" is wrong — "which" is used for things; for a person we use "who" (correctly already in the sentence).

• Option 2 "lot of gifts by him" changes "for" to "by", which is incorrect.

• Option 4 "and her sister" wrongly changes "his" — the aunt brought gifts for him and his sister (the boy's sister).

NOTE

• Prepositions of place: use "in" for large areas (in America, in Delhi, in a country); "at" for a specific point (at the bus stop, at the door).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

Sushant looked blue in the face after the marathon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. exhausted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "blue in the face" means completely exhausted / drained of energy after great effort (also used for making an effort until one is worn out). After a marathon, Sushant was thoroughly tired. (अत्यधिक थका हुआ)

◦ Example: I argued until I was blue in the face, but he would not listen.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "happy", 2 "sad" and 4 "good" do not capture the sense of extreme tiredness/exertion.

NOTE

• Do not confuse with "feeling blue", which means feeling sad. "Blue in the face" specifically implies exhaustion/great strain.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

She finally spilled the beans about the surprise party.
option_3: Revealed a secret or disclosed information
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Revealed a secret or disclosed information.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "spill the beans" means to reveal a secret or disclose confidential information, often accidentally. (राज़ खोल देना)

◦ Example: Don't tell Riya the plan — she always spills the beans.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are literal or unrelated interpretations and do not convey the idiomatic meaning.

NOTE

• Similar idioms about revealing secrets: "let the cat out of the bag", "give the game away", "blow the whistle".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

After the floods, Uttarakhand was in a _______(ravaged) condition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. restored.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ravaged" means severely damaged / devastated / destroyed. Its antonym is "restored", meaning brought back to a good/original condition; repaired. (नष्ट किया गया का विलोम — पुनर्स्थापित)

◦ Example: The flood ravaged the town, but years later it was fully restored.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "ratified" (formally approved) and Option 4 "influenced" (affected) are unrelated.

• Option 2 "languid" (weak/sluggish) is not the opposite of "ravaged".

NOTE

• Synonyms of ravaged: devastated, destroyed, wrecked, ruined. Antonyms: restored, repaired, rebuilt, renovated.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

If she had gone to the party, she could have met Amit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No substitution required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is a third conditional (an unreal/imaginary situation in the past): "If + subject + had + past participle (V3), ... could/would/might have + V3".

◦ Correct (as given): If she had gone to the party, she could have met Amit.

• "had gone" (had + past participle of go) is perfectly correct, so no substitution is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "had go" is wrong — after "had" we need the past participle (gone), not the base form "go".

• Option 3 "have went" is doubly wrong ("went" is not a past participle).

• Option 4 "has gone" (present perfect) does not fit the third-conditional structure.

NOTE

• Third conditional pattern: If + had + V3, ... would/could/might have + V3 (used for past hypothetical situations).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

Commodity prices are the dearer in the present economic scenario.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. dearest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The article "the" is used with the superlative degree, not the comparative. So "the dearer" (comparative) should be "the dearest" (superlative), meaning most expensive. (सबसे महँगा)

◦ Correct: Commodity prices are the dearest in the present economic scenario.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "quite dear" and Option 2 "dear" (positive degree) do not go with "the".

• Option 4 "No substitution" is wrong because "the dearer" is grammatically incorrect.

NOTE

• Degrees of "dear" (= expensive): dear – dearer (with "than") – the dearest (with "the"). "The" always pairs with the superlative.

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

We do not expet Reema to follow all the rules from the first day of work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. expect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt word is "expect", meaning to think or believe that something will happen; to anticipate. (अपेक्षा करना)

◦ Correct: We do not expect Reema to follow all the rules from the first day of work.

• Spelling key: EX + PECT.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "expict", "expact" and "execpt" are all misspelt.

• Do not confuse "expect" (anticipate) with "except" (apart from) — they are different words.

NOTE

• Related words: expect (verb), expectation (noun), expectant (adjective), expected/unexpected.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Something that is so extraordinary or unbelievable that it's hard to believe it
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Incredible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Incredible" means too extraordinary or unlikely to be believed; unbelievable. (अविश्वसनीय)

◦ Example: The magician performed an incredible trick that no one could explain.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Horrible" (very unpleasant), Option 3 "Ordinary" (normal/common) and Option 4 "Exquisite" (extremely beautiful/delicate) do not mean "hard to believe".

NOTE

• The prefix "in-" here means "not"; "credible" = believable, so "incredible" = not believable. Related: credible, credit, credulous, incredulous.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who abstains from any sort of alcoholic drinks
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Teetotaller.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Teetotaller" is a person who never drinks alcohol / completely abstains from alcoholic drinks. (शराब से पूर्ण परहेज़ करने वाला व्यक्ति)

◦ Example: Being a strict teetotaller, he refused even a sip of wine.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Termagant" (a bad-tempered, quarrelsome woman), Option 2 "Veteran" (a person with long experience) and Option 4 "Samaritan" (a person who helps others selflessly) do not fit.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: Teetotaller (abstains from alcohol), Ascetic (abstains from worldly pleasures), Epicure (fond of good food and drink).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Alaska in the USA / is the colder / of all the states.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. is the colder.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "of all the states" indicates a comparison among many states, which requires the superlative degree — "the coldest", not the comparative "the colder".

◦ Correct: Alaska in the USA is the coldest of all the states.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Alaska in the USA" and "of all the states" are correct.

• The comparative "colder" is used only when comparing two items (with "than").

NOTE

• Degrees of "cold": cold – colder (two things, with "than") – the coldest (three or more, with "the / of all"). "Of all the ..." always signals the superlative.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The team worked together to execute the challenging task.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. accomplish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Execute" (here) means to carry out / perform / complete a task. Its closest synonym is "accomplish" (to achieve or complete successfully). (पूरा करना / निष्पादित करना)

◦ Example: The engineers executed/accomplished the project ahead of schedule.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "analyse" (to examine in detail), Option 3 "announce" (to make public) and Option 4 "abandon" (to give up/leave) do not match.

NOTE

• Synonyms of execute (carry out): accomplish, perform, implement, carry out, fulfil. Note "execute" also has a second meaning — "to put to death".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Aresst.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aresst" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Arrest", meaning to seize/detain someone by legal authority; to stop. (गिरफ़्तार करना)

◦ Correct spelling: A-R-R-E-S-T (double "r", single "s").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Express" (to convey / a fast train), "Excess" (too much) and "Harass" (to trouble/annoy repeatedly) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Watch the doubling: arrest has "rr" not "ss"; harass has one "r" and double "s". Careful spelling of such words is frequently tested in SSC exams.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel (1)_____ fore-and-aft rigging on the mainmast and square rigging on the foremast. The pirates that (2)______ the Mediterranean in the sixteenth century loved it for its speed and ease of handling. The brigantine (3)_________ into a true sailing vessel in the waters of northern Europe. Although the words began to be used interchangeably, it was (4)_______ from the fully square-rigged brig by its gaff-rigged mainsail. True brigantines, for (5)_____, were defined as having square topsails above a gaffed mainsail.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. featuring.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Featuring" means having as a prominent characteristic / including. The brigantine is described as a vessel featuring fore-and-aft rigging on the mainmast and square rigging on the foremast. (विशेषता रखते हुए)

◦ Correct: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel featuring fore-and-aft rigging ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "focusing" (concentrating on), Option 2 "predicting" (foretelling) and Option 3 "attending" (being present at) do not fit the sense of "having/possessing" a physical feature.

NOTE

• "Feature" as a verb = to have or include something as an important part (a car featuring airbags, a phone featuring a big screen).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel (1)_____ fore-and-aft rigging on the mainmast and square rigging on the foremast. The pirates that (2)______ the Mediterranean in the sixteenth century loved it for its speed and ease of handling. The brigantine (3)_________ into a true sailing vessel in the waters of northern Europe. Although the words began to be used interchangeably, it was (4)_______ from the fully square-rigged brig by its gaff-rigged mainsail. True brigantines, for (5)_____, were defined as having square topsails above a gaffed mainsail.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ravaged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ravaged" means plundered, raided and caused destruction. The pirates who ravaged the Mediterranean (raided/looted it) loved the brigantine for its speed. This fits the action of pirates. (लूटपाट/तबाही मचाना)

◦ Correct: The pirates that ravaged the Mediterranean in the sixteenth century loved it ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "transpired" (happened / became known), Option 2 "integrated" (combined) and Option 4 "fixed" (repaired/fastened) do not suit the destructive activity of pirates on a sea.

NOTE

• Synonyms of ravage: plunder, devastate, pillage, lay waste. Pirates "ravaging" or "plundering" the seas is a natural collocation.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel (1)_____ fore-and-aft rigging on the mainmast and square rigging on the foremast. The pirates that (2)______ the Mediterranean in the sixteenth century loved it for its speed and ease of handling. The brigantine (3)_________ into a true sailing vessel in the waters of northern Europe. Although the words began to be used interchangeably, it was (4)_______ from the fully square-rigged brig by its gaff-rigged mainsail. True brigantines, for (5)_____, were defined as having square topsails above a gaffed mainsail.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. evolved.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Evolved" means developed gradually into a more advanced/different form. The brigantine evolved into a true sailing vessel in the waters of northern Europe. (विकसित हुआ)

◦ Correct: The brigantine evolved into a true sailing vessel in the waters of northern Europe.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "submitted" (yielded / handed in), Option 2 "discharged" (released) and Option 4 "garnished" (decorated food) do not convey gradual development.

NOTE

• "Evolve into" is a common collocation meaning to change and develop over time (the startup evolved into a large company). Synonyms: develop, transform, grow, mature.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel (1)_____ fore-and-aft rigging on the mainmast and square rigging on the foremast. The pirates that (2)______ the Mediterranean in the sixteenth century loved it for its speed and ease of handling. The brigantine (3)_________ into a true sailing vessel in the waters of northern Europe. Although the words began to be used interchangeably, it was (4)_______ from the fully square-rigged brig by its gaff-rigged mainsail. True brigantines, for (5)_____, were defined as having square topsails above a gaffed mainsail.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. join (as per the official answer key).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The official answer key marks Option 4 "join" as the correct response for blank number 4.

• The sentence contrasts the brigantine with the fully square-rigged brig, the two being distinguished by the brigantine's gaff-rigged mainsail.

◦ As printed with the keyed option: ... it was join from the fully square-rigged brig by its gaff-rigged mainsail.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "mourned" (grieved) and Option 3 "spill" (to let liquid flow over) clearly do not fit the context.

• Option 1 "split" carries a sense of separation; however, the official key records the answer as Option 4 "join", and the printed key is treated as authoritative.

NOTE

• In SSC papers the printed "Correct Answer" is the official key and is recorded as given. Here the key marks join (Option 4).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel (1)_____ fore-and-aft rigging on the mainmast and square rigging on the foremast. The pirates that (2)______ the Mediterranean in the sixteenth century loved it for its speed and ease of handling. The brigantine (3)_________ into a true sailing vessel in the waters of northern Europe. Although the words began to be used interchangeably, it was (4)_______ from the fully square-rigged brig by its gaff-rigged mainsail. True brigantines, for (5)_____, were defined as having square topsails above a gaffed mainsail.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. instance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed phrase "for instance" means for example. It is used to introduce a specific example (here, the definition of "true brigantines"). (उदाहरण के लिए)

◦ Correct: True brigantines, for instance, were defined as having square topsails above a gaffed mainsail.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "mention", Option 3 "case" and Option 4 "location" do not form the standard example-introducing phrase.

• "for case" and "for location" are not idiomatic; only "for instance" (= for example) works here.

NOTE

• Expressions meaning "for example": for instance, for example, e.g., such as, to illustrate. "For instance" is set off by commas.

question: Which of following silver coins was introduced by Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tanka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sultan Shamsuddin Iltutmish (of the Delhi Sultanate's Slave/Mamluk dynasty) introduced the silver "Tanka" and the copper "Jital", laying the basis of the Sultanate's coinage system. (चाँदी का टंका — इल्तुतमिश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The silver tanka later became the standard silver coin, and the rupee of the Mughals evolved from this tradition.

• Iltutmish (r. 1211–1236) was the real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate; he completed the Qutub Minar and set up the Iqta system.

NOTE

• Iltutmish also organised the "Chahalgani/Chalisa" — a group of forty powerful Turkish nobles. His coins bore his name and titles in Arabic.

question: Wasifuddin Dagar was associated with which of the following classical music genres?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dhrupad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Wasifuddin Dagar is a renowned exponent of "Dhrupad", one of the oldest forms of Hindustani classical vocal music. He belongs to the celebrated Dagar family (Dagarvani gharana). (ध्रुपद — वासिफुद्दीन डागर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Dhrupad is a solemn, devotional and highly structured style, older than Khyal; it emphasises the pure elaboration of the raga (alap) and rhythmic patterns.

• The Dagar family has preserved the Dhrupad tradition for many generations.

NOTE

• Major Hindustani vocal styles: Dhrupad, Khyal, Thumri, Tarana and Ghazal. Dhrupad is considered the most ancient and austere among them.

question: When was the Lahore declaration signed between India and Pakistan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is February 1999.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Lahore Declaration" was signed between India and Pakistan in February 1999 (on 21 February 1999), by Prime Ministers Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Nawaz Sharif. (लाहौर घोषणा — फरवरी 1999)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• It followed Vajpayee's historic Delhi–Lahore bus journey and aimed at reducing the risk of nuclear conflict and improving bilateral ties.

• The spirit of the declaration was soon undermined by the Kargil War (May–July 1999).

NOTE

• Key India–Pakistan agreements: Tashkent Agreement (1966), Shimla Agreement (1972) and Lahore Declaration (1999).

question: According to Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2022, what was the population of the poor in India in 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 228.9 million.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2022 (released by UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative, OPHI), the number of multidimensionally poor people in India in 2020 was about 228.9 million. (बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2022)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The MPI measures poverty across three dimensions — health, education and standard of living — using ten indicators.

• The report noted that India had significantly reduced its poverty over the years.

NOTE

• India also publishes its own National MPI through NITI Aayog, aligned with the global methodology, tracking deprivations in health, education and living standards.

question: The part of a temple wherein the main deity of the temple is housed is known as the _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Garbha Griha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Garbha Griha" (literally the "womb chamber") is the innermost sanctum of a Hindu temple where the main deity (idol) is housed. (गर्भगृह — मुख्य देवता का स्थान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shikhara — the towering spire built above the garbha griha (in North Indian/Nagara temples).

• Mandapa — the pillared hall in front of the sanctum where devotees gather.

• Stupa — a Buddhist dome-shaped structure containing relics (not a part of a Hindu temple).

NOTE

• Temple architecture styles in India: Nagara (North), Dravida (South, with a gopuram gateway and vimana tower) and Vesara (a blend of both).

question: Sama Chakeva is a folk dance based on the mythological story of the siblings Sama and Chakeva, in which the brother goes to an extreme extent to save his sister. With which State of India is this folk dance associated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sama Chakeva" is a traditional folk dance/festival of the Mithila region of Bihar (also popular in parts of Nepal and Jharkhand). It celebrates the bond between brother and sister through the mythological story of Sama and Chakeva. (सामा-चकेवा — बिहार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It is celebrated mainly by women during the Kartik month (November) and involves making clay figures of birds and singing folk songs.

• It reflects the theme of sibling love, similar in spirit to Raksha Bandhan and Bhai Dooj.

NOTE

• Folk dances of Bihar: Jat-Jatin, Sama Chakeva, Jhijhian, Bidesia and Paika.

question: Which of the following is an autobiography of LK Advani?
solution_text:
The correct answer is My Country My Life.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "My Country My Life" is the autobiography of veteran politician and former Deputy Prime Minister Lal Krishna Advani (L. K. Advani), published in 2008. (माई कंट्री माई लाइफ — एल. के. आडवाणी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Exam Warriors — written by Narendra Modi.

• Wings of Fire — autobiography of Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

• Dare to Dream — a biography associated with Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam / on his life and ideas.

NOTE

• L. K. Advani was a founder-leader of the BJP, led the Ram Rath Yatra (1990), and served as Home Minister and Deputy PM in the Vajpayee government. He was awarded the Bharat Ratna (2024).

question: The 'Rule of Law' is a key feature of the Indian Constitution which is a doctrine ascribed to ____________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Albert Venn Dicey.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The doctrine of the "Rule of Law" is ascribed to the British jurist Albert Venn Dicey (A. V. Dicey), who expounded it in his book "Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution (1885)". (विधि का शासन — ए. वी. डायसी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Dicey identified three elements of the Rule of Law: (i) supremacy of law, (ii) equality before the law, and (iii) the predominance of the legal spirit (rights coming from judicial decisions).

• The concept is enshrined in the Indian Constitution mainly through Article 14 (equality before law and equal protection of laws).

NOTE

• The Rule of Law is part of the basic structure of the Constitution and ensures that no one is above the law and that the government itself is bound by law.

question: Who among the following Governor Generals of India wrote about the predicament of Indian weavers, “The bones of the cotton weavers are scattered on the plains of India”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord William Bentinck.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lord William Bentinck (Governor-General, 1828–1835) famously remarked on the ruin of Indian handloom weavers: "The bones of the cotton weavers are bleaching the plains of India", describing the devastation caused by cheap British machine-made cloth. (लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bentinck introduced major social reforms — the abolition of Sati (1829) with Raja Ram Mohan Roy's support, and the suppression of Thuggee.

• On Macaulay's recommendation, he promoted English education in India (1835).

NOTE

• Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India (under the Charter Act of 1833); earlier the post was Governor-General of Bengal.

question: The Dudhsagar waterfall is a major tourist place of ________ State.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Dudhsagar Waterfall" (meaning "sea of milk") is a major tourist attraction located on the Mandovi River in the state of Goa, on the Goa–Karnataka border in the Western Ghats. (दूधसागर जलप्रपात — गोवा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is one of India's tallest waterfalls (about 310 m) and lies within the Bhagwan Mahaveer Sanctuary and Mollem National Park.

• The falls appear as a cascade of white foamy water resembling milk, hence the name.

NOTE

• Other famous waterfalls of India: Kunchikal (Karnataka), Jog Falls (Karnataka), Nohkalikai (Meghalaya), Athirappilly (Kerala).

question: Who became the first woman to win two gold medals in a single Para Asian Games event in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sheetal Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sheetal Devi, the para-archer from Jammu and Kashmir, became the first woman to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games (Hangzhou, 2023). (शीतल देवी — पैरा तीरंदाज़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sheetal Devi, born with phocomelia (undeveloped arms), shoots the bow using her legs and feet, and is one of the world's few armless archers competing internationally.

• She won golds in the women's individual compound and mixed team compound events.

NOTE

• Sheetal Devi is a rising icon of Indian para-sport and was later honoured with the Arjuna Award.

question: In the periodic table, what is the trend for atomic radius as you move from left to right across a period (horizontal row)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Atomic radius decreases.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As we move from left to right across a period, the atomic radius decreases. This is because the nuclear charge (number of protons) increases while electrons are added to the same shell, so the nucleus pulls the electrons in more strongly. (परमाणु त्रिज्या घटती है)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Down a group, the atomic radius increases because new electron shells are added, increasing the distance of the outermost electrons from the nucleus.

• Trends across a period: atomic radius decreases, ionisation energy increases, electronegativity increases, metallic character decreases.

NOTE

• The modern periodic law (Henry Moseley) states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic numbers.

question: Gulabo Sapera, a legendry folk dancer from Kalbeliya tribe, Rajasthan, received Padma Shri in the year ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2016.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gulabo Sapera, the celebrated Kalbeliya dancer from Rajasthan, was awarded the Padma Shri in 2016 for her contribution to art. (गुलाबो सपेरा — पद्म श्री 2016)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Kalbeliya dance, performed by the Kalbeliya (snake-charmer) community, was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

• The graceful, serpent-like movements of the dancers give the dance its distinctive character.

NOTE

• The Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India, after the Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan.

question: Which of the following white papers, released by NITI Aayog, is related to Public Health Surveillance in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vision 2035.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vision 2035: Public Health Surveillance in India" is the white paper released by NITI Aayog that lays out a roadmap to strengthen India's public health surveillance system. (विज़न 2035 — नीति आयोग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It aims to make India's surveillance system responsive and predictive, integrating it with the Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres and using data and technology.

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission in 2015; its chairperson is the Prime Minister.

NOTE

• Public health surveillance became especially important after the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting the need for early detection and rapid response systems.

question: Who amongst the following said that the government fiscal policy should be used to stabilise the level of output and employment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is JM Keynes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• John Maynard Keynes (J. M. Keynes) argued that the government's fiscal policy (taxation and public spending) should be used to stabilise the level of output and employment, especially during depressions. (जे. एम. कीन्स — राजकोषीय नीति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Keynes's famous work is "The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money (1936)", written after the Great Depression of 1929.

• He is regarded as the father of modern macroeconomics and advocated government intervention to boost demand.

NOTE

• Adam Smith — father of economics ("Wealth of Nations"); Alfred Marshall — "Principles of Economics"; Lionel Robbins — famous scarcity definition of economics.

question: Which of the following options is an example of a decomposer in an ecosystem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fungus.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Fungus" is a decomposer — it breaks down dead plants and animals and returns nutrients to the soil. (कवक — अपघटक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Decomposers (e.g., fungi and bacteria) are called saprotrophs; they recycle nutrients back into the ecosystem.

• Producers (green plants) make food by photosynthesis; herbivores eat plants; carnivores eat other animals.

NOTE

• Ecosystem components: Producers → Primary consumers (herbivores) → Secondary/Tertiary consumers (carnivores) → Decomposers. Decomposers complete the nutrient cycle.

question: Who among the following social reformers wrote Brahmo Covenant which was a statement of the creed of the Brahmo Samaj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Debendranath Tagore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Debendranath Tagore wrote the "Brahmo Covenant (Brahmo Dharma)", a statement of the creed/principles of the Brahmo Samaj. He reorganised and revitalised the Samaj after Raja Ram Mohan Roy. (देवेंद्रनाथ टैगोर — ब्रह्म समाज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj in 1828 (as Brahmo Sabha); Debendranath Tagore joined it and later led it, founding the Tattvabodhini Sabha.

• Debendranath Tagore was the father of the poet Rabindranath Tagore.

• Keshab Chandra Sen later led a more radical faction of the Brahmo Samaj.

NOTE

• The Brahmo Samaj opposed idol worship, the caste system and social evils like Sati, and promoted monotheism and social reform.

question: In which of the following states is the famous International Sand Art Festival organised, where artists get enthralled by the diverse thoughts and their elucidation on sand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous "International Sand Art Festival" is organised annually at Chandrabhaga Beach, Konark, in Odisha. (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सैंड आर्ट फेस्टिवल — ओडिशा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• It is held alongside the Konark Festival in December, attracting sand artists from India and abroad.

• Odisha's Sudarsan Pattnaik is a world-renowned sand artist who has won many international awards.

NOTE

• Odisha's cultural landmarks: the Sun Temple at Konark (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), the Jagannath Temple at Puri, and the Odissi classical dance.

question: Which sector uses the groundwater maximally?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Agriculture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Agriculture" sector uses groundwater maximally in India — most of the extracted groundwater is used for irrigation. (कृषि क्षेत्र — भूजल का सर्वाधिक उपयोग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• India is the largest user of groundwater in the world; agriculture accounts for roughly 80–90% of groundwater use.

• Over-extraction (especially through tube wells) has led to falling water tables in states like Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.

NOTE

• The Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) monitors and manages groundwater; schemes like Atal Bhujal Yojana promote sustainable groundwater management.

question: The black coating formed on silver jewellery is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ag2S.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The black coating on silver articles/jewellery is silver sulphide (Ag₂S). It forms when silver reacts with hydrogen sulphide (H₂S) present in air (tarnishing/corrosion of silver). (सिल्वर सल्फाइड — Ag₂S)

◦ Reaction: 2Ag + H₂S → Ag₂S + H₂.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Similarly, copper develops a green coating of basic copper carbonate, and iron forms rust (hydrated iron oxide).

• Silver ornaments are cleaned to remove this black tarnish and restore shine.

NOTE

• Common compounds: AgNO₃ (silver nitrate, used in photography), AgCl (silver chloride), Ag₂CO₃ (silver carbonate). Only Ag₂S is the black tarnish on silver.

question: The Megalithic site __________ is a site on the river Ghod, a tributary of the Bhima.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Inamgaon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inamgaon" is an archaeological (Chalcolithic/megalithic) site located on the banks of the Ghod River, a tributary of the Bhima River, in Maharashtra. (इनामगाँव — घोड नदी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Inamgaon was a major settlement of the Jorwe culture (a Chalcolithic culture of the Deccan) and gives evidence of farming, houses, and burial practices.

• The people practised agriculture and animal domestication and used black-and-red ware pottery.

NOTE

• Other important prehistoric/megalithic sites: Hire Benakal, Hallur (Karnataka) and Brahmagiri; Inamgaon is a key site for understanding Deccan Chalcolithic life.

question: Which of the following crops takes almost a year to grow?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sugarcane.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sugarcane" is a long-duration crop that takes almost a year (about 10–18 months) to mature. (गन्ना — लगभग एक वर्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sugarcane is a tropical/subtropical, Kharif-season crop needing hot, humid climate and plenty of water; Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra are leading producers.

• It is the main source of sugar, gur (jaggery) and khandsari, and the byproduct bagasse is used for making paper and generating power.

NOTE

• Short-duration crops like ragi, soybean and groundnut mature in a few months; sugarcane is distinct for its long growing period.

question: The strength of Supreme Court has increased to how many judges as of 13 Feb 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 34.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of 13 February 2023, the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court of India stood at 34 judges — that is, 1 Chief Justice of India + 33 other judges. (उच्चतम न्यायालय — 34 न्यायाधीश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The strength was raised from 31 to 34 by the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019.

• Article 124 of the Constitution provides for the establishment of the Supreme Court; Parliament can fix the number of judges by law.

NOTE

• Supreme Court judges hold office until the age of 65 years; High Court judges retire at 62 years.

question: Which state received the Sportstar ACES Best State for the Promotion of Sport award in 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tamil Nadu received the "Sportstar ACES Best State for the Promotion of Sport" award in 2024, recognising its efforts in developing sports infrastructure and talent. (तमिलनाडु — 2024)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Sportstar ACES Awards are presented by Sportstar magazine (of The Hindu Group) to honour India's top athletes and sporting achievements.

• Tamil Nadu has actively promoted sport through its state sports policy and events like the Khelo India initiatives.

NOTE

• Khelo India and the National Sports Awards (Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna, Arjuna Award, Dronacharya Award) are key platforms for promoting sports in India.

question: The legislative powers in India are divided into three lists, which are the Union List, the State List and the _____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Concurrent List.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legislative powers in India are divided into three lists in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution: the Union List, the State List and the Concurrent List. (समवर्ती सूची — Concurrent List)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Union List — subjects on which only Parliament can legislate (e.g., defence, foreign affairs, currency).

• State List — subjects for State legislatures (e.g., police, public health, agriculture).

• Concurrent List — subjects on which both Centre and States can legislate (e.g., education, marriage, forests); in case of conflict, central law prevails.

NOTE

• This three-fold division is given in the Seventh Schedule (Article 246); the scheme was borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935. Residuary powers rest with the Union.
